title: Ruby: Arrays and Hashes
description: Write a Ruby program demonstrating arrays, hashes, and common iteration methods.

codeTemplate.rb:
# Arrays
numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
puts "Original: #{numbers}"
puts "Doubled: #{numbers.map { |n| n * 2 }}"
puts "Evens: #{numbers.select { |n| n.even? }}"
puts "Sum: #{numbers.sum}"

# Hashes
person = { name: 'Alice', age: 30, city: 'New York' }
puts "\nPerson: #{person}"
puts "Name: #{person[:name]}"
person[:job] = 'Engineer'
puts "Updated: #{person}"

# Iteration
puts "\nFruits:"
%w[apple banana cherry].each_with_index do |f, i|
  puts "  #{i + 1}. #{f}"
end

# Ranges
puts "\nRange 1..5: #{(1..5).to_a}"
puts "Sum 1 to 10: #{(1..10).sum}"

verificationTest: output.includes('Original: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]') && output.includes('Sum: 15') && output.includes('Name: Alice') && output.includes('Sum 1 to 10: 55')
hints: Arrays use square brackets, hashes use curly braces with `=>` or `:` syntax
Use `map`, `select`, `each` for iteration instead of for loops
Symbols `:name` are lightweight identifiers often used as hash keys
`%w[]` creates an array of strings from whitespace-separated words
